hyps.why: At tiny learning rates the network is undertrained after 243 epochs, so raising the rate gives large gains compared with the already-adequate mid/high rates.
At learning rates near 0.278-1 Adam becomes unstable, so a further increase hurts more than it does elsewhere.
Larger batches mean fewer updates, which compounds undertraining when the learning rate is already tiny.
Smaller batches give more update steps, which helps a lot when the learning rate is too low to converge.
Small batches with a very high learning rate produce noisy, unstable gradients that damage accuracy.
Wider networks have larger effective step sizes and diverge more easily at high learning rates.
Deeper ReLU networks are more fragile at high learning rates, so adding a layer hurts more there.
Alpha of 0.129-1 over-regularizes the weights, so increasing it further causes underfitting.
Going from very narrow to moderate width adds capacity and gives larger gains than going wider when the network is already wide.
With large batches there are few updates per epoch, so a higher learning rate is needed to converge.
